title: Borrow strength without borrowing future labels

blocks.text: A category with one positive example has a raw target mean of one. That does not establish that every future member of the category will be positive. Smoothing pulls uncertain category estimates toward a broader baseline. The formula behaves as if each group received lambda additional observations whose average target equals the global training mean.

Fit a smoothed target-encoding dictionary: each category mean is shrunk toward the global mean by smoothing pseudo-observations. Return the mapping and fallback global mean. Fit only on the training fold.

A categorical feature records a group such as a product type. Target encoding maps that group to a target statistic. A training fold supplies fitting data; a validation fold measures generalization. Using validation labels to create validation features leaks the answer.

The animation compares category A, which has three observations, with category B, which has one. Both are pulled toward the same global mean, but B moves more because the pseudo-observations are a larger fraction of its effective count. Turn smoothing off to recover raw group means. Turn it on to see the relative effect of group size.

blocks.text: Connect the picture to the mathematics

blocks.caption: s_c is the category target sum, n_c is its count, mu is the global training mean, and lambda is the nonnegative smoothing strength.

blocks.text: The function returns a dictionary and a fallback mean. A later transformation looks up known categories and uses the fallback for unseen categories. It must not recompute statistics from validation or test labels. This function fits statistics only; the caller must ensure that the rows passed into it belong to the training fold.

Even using all training labels to encode the same training rows can create self-label leakage, especially for rare categories. A common remedy is cross-fitting: encode each training fold using statistics from other folds, then fit a final mapping on all training data for inference. The supplied helper does not implement that outer process. Distinguish this limitation from validation leakage, which occurs when evaluation labels enter fitting at all. Check rare groups, unseen groups, zero smoothing, and the global fallback explicitly.
blocks.title: The boundary of this implementation

notes.text: The fallback and prior mean must be learned only from eligible training rows.
The numerator combines observed target mass and smoothing pseudo-observations.

blocks.text: The original solution is preserved. The diagrams use deliberately small examples to expose the mechanism. Passing these checks is evidence for these examples, not an exhaustive correctness proof.

q122-new-case.prompt: A group has target sum 2, count 4, global mean 0.5, and smoothing 6. What is its encoding?

explanation.correct: (2+6×0.5)/(4+6)=5/10=0.5. Its local rate already equals the global mean.
explanation.default: Revisit the stated quantities and units. (2+6×0.5)/(4+6)=5/10=0.5. Its local rate already equals the global mean.

q122-prediction.prompt: A group has one success out of one observation, global mean 0.5, and smoothing 4. What is its encoded value?

explanation.default: Revisit the stated quantities and units. (1+4×0.5)/(1+4)=3/5=0.6.
